guards.stops: The `proof: Proof` handler argument is cast before the body runs. A redeemer that is not Constr 0 with exactly three bytestrings aborts, even when the datum is missing or isn't a Register, so the 'anyone can spend' branches still need a well-formed Proof. This matches proofOf (definitions.lean:15-18) and its `none => False` (definitions.lean:38).
guards.test: W11 accepts; W12 (2 fields), W13 (4 fields), W14 (tag 1), W15 (an I field), W16 (I 0) and W26 (datum I 5 with redeemer I 0) reject. Runner: work/V1/tools/runs.py, cross-checked by work/V1/tools/haskell_runs.py.

guards.stops: list.has(extra_signatories, vkh): a valid proof cannot be replayed without the one-time key's signature.
guards.test: W2 rejects (vkh not a signer); W3 accepts (vkh third of three signers).

guards.stops: expect Some(z) on from_bytearray_big_endian: z_b must decode below q, so the alias z+q (the same point) is refused. Leading zero bytes are still accepted, in both the source and schnorrProve.
The challenge binds g ‖ g_r ‖ u ‖ vkh in that order and decodes it big-endian. A proof made for another order or for a little-endian challenge fails.
guards.test: W7 (challenge order g‖u‖g_r) and W8 (little-endian c) reject; W1 accepts.

guards.stops: expect [(pid, tkn, amt)] = flatten(mint), in both arms: exactly one asset line in the whole mint, across every policy.
guards.test: P6 (an extra asset of another policy), P25 (two names under the own policy) and P19 (empty mint) reject.

guards.stops: bytearray.push(txid, idx) is consByteString, which aborts outside 0..255 under V3 semantics. No rollover to a duplicate name, matching the source's rollover_attack test.
guards.test: P16 (first input index 256, name built from index 0) rejects under the V3 variants C and E but accepts under the pre-V3 variants A and B (work/V1/runs/hs/P16.flat).

guards.stops: bytearray.take(tkn, 4) == #5eed0e1f on burns: slicing clamps, so a name shorter than 4 bytes can't match.
guards.test: P10 (3-byte name) and P13 (another policy) reject; P8 and P9 (exactly 5eed0e1f) accept.

checked_ok: The source is the deployed code. v1/source built offline with Aiken v1.1.9 and the given stdlib v2.2.0, with the seed 44acabcafe applied, reproduces wallet 94bca9c0…, seedelf 84967d91… and always_false 6777ba4d… byte for byte. Those are also the bytes in seedelf-verification/Seedelf/Scripts/*.hex that the theorems import. So each reading of 'how Aiken compiles this' below comes from the decoded deployed program: work/V1/scripts/wallet.r.uplc and seedelf.r.uplc.

Wallet purpose. wallet.ak:20 (spend) and 64-66 (else fail) match definitions.lean:28-29 and 39. Compiled: ScriptInfo tag 1 or error (wallet.r.uplc:19, 251-252). W27 (minting) and W28 (rewarding) reject. Matches.

Wallet redeemer. wallet.ak:22 `proof: Proof` is a strict cast: tag 0 or error (wallet.r.uplc:29), three unBData heads (:31-36), and the remaining tail must be empty or error (:38-39, 242). Extra fields and a wrong constructor index both abort. This matches proofOf, Constr 0 with exactly [B, B, B] (definitions.lean:15-18), and the field order Proof{z_b, g_r_b, vkh} (schnorr.ak:20-27). Matches.

Wallet evaluation order. Aiken casts the redeemer before the body, so a missing or non-Register datum still needs a well-formed Proof. definitions.lean:30-38 matches proofOf before the datum. W26 rejects, W11 accepts. Matches.

Wallet datum. wallet.ak:21, 28-29 and 59, `Option<Data>` with Some/None, matches definitions.lean:32-37. The typed Option encodes as Constr 0 [d] / Constr 1 [] (CardanoLedgerApi IsData/Class.lean:43-48), and V2.Datum = Data. Compiled: tag 0 continues, otherwise True (wallet.r.uplc:41, 240-241). A missing datum gives True. Matches.

Wallet soft cast. wallet.ak:30 and 50-55, `if register is Register` else True. Compiled (wallet.r.uplc:46-88): chooseData must be Constr, tag 0, a first field that is B, a second field that is B, and no third field. Every other shape falls to True, never to an error. That is exactly registerOf, Constr 0 [B g, B u] (definitions.lean:21-24), with `none => True` (:36). Neither side checks the bytestring lengths. W17 (an extra field), W18 (tag 1), W19, W20, W21, W22, W23 and W24 all accept with a junk proof; W25 (a real Register with a junk proof) rejects. Matches.

Wallet conjunction. wallet.ak:38-49 `and { prove?, list.has? }` matches definitions.lean:35. Short-circuiting can't change the verdict, because list.has can't abort on a typed context. The prove arguments (generator, public_value, z_b, g_r_b, vkh) are wired as schnorrProve g u z gr vkh (compiled :171-175). Matches.

Wallet signer check. wallet.ak:48 list.has(extra_signatories, vkh) (list.ak:240-250) matches `vkh ∈ txInfoSignatories` (definitions.lean:35). Compiled: an equalsByteString loop (wallet.r.uplc:181-205) over TxInfo field 8 (:206-214), and the V3 TxInfo encoding puts the signatories at index 8 as Data.List of B (V1/Contexts.lean:430-445). W2 rejects, W3 accepts. Matches.

schnorrProve step 1. schnorr.ak:102 `expect Some(z) = from_bytearray_big_endian(z_b)` is new(bytearray_to_integer(True, z_b)) with 0 ≤ n < field_prime (scalar.ak:22-23, 40-46, 57-59). It matches definitions.lean:8 and 10, with bigEndian (:85). byteStringToInteger true is big-endian (Bitwise/Basic.lean:84-91; the Opaque alias is Bitwise.lean:51-59). q (:89) equals the stdlib field_prime, the program's constant (wallet.r.uplc:159) and the BLS12-381 group order r. W5 accepts, W6 rejects. Matches.

schnorrProve step 2. schnorr.ak:103 g_z = scale(decompress(generator), z) = scalarMul(z, uncompress g) (g1.ak:70-72, 98-100). It matches `.ok G` and `scalarMul zi G` (definitions.lean:6-7, 11). W10 (bad generator bytes) rejects. Matches.

schnorrProve step 3. schnorr.ak:30-46 and 106-108: c = big-endian blake2b_224(((g ‖ g_r) ‖ u) ‖ vkh), because bytearray.concat(left, right) is append(left, right) and `a |> concat(b)` is concat(a, b). It matches challenge g u gr vkh = blake2b_224(append(append(append g gr) u) vkh) (definitions.lean:80-81), decoded with bigEndian (:9-10). Compiled: wallet.r.uplc:112-126. The c < q check passes on both sides, since 28 bytes < 2^224 < q. W7 and W8 reject. Matches.

schnorrProve steps 4-5. schnorr.ak:111 and 115: u_c = scale(decompress(public_value), c), then equal(g_z, add(decompress(g_r_b), u_c)). This matches `.ok U`, `.ok R` and bls12_381_G1_equal (scalarMul zi G) (add R (scalarMul c U)) (definitions.lean:6-7, 11), with the same operand order as the program (wallet.r.uplc:129-142). W1 accepts; W4 (z+1) and W9 (g_r not a point) reject. Matches.

schnorrProve error versus false. Where the source aborts (z outside [0, q), a point that doesn't decompress, c outside [0, q)), schnorrProve returns false (definitions.lean:12). walletAccepts only uses `= true`, and the V3 wrapper turns both a False result and an abort into rejection (wallet.r.uplc:13, 253-256). The source checks z before any decompression, but that order can't change accept versus reject. So schnorrProve is what schnorr.ak computes, step by step. Its builtins are the same opaque functions the CEK model calls (G1.lean:31-47, Hash/Basic.lean:37-38). The uncompress model checks the 48-byte length, the compression, infinity and sign flags, the field range, findY and subgroup membership (Cryptograph/BLS12_381/Basic.lean:814-834).

Policy purpose and redeemer. seedelf.ak:19 (mint) and 77-79 (else fail) match definitions.lean:58-59 and 69. The `personal_tag: ByteArray` cast is unBData (seedelf.r.uplc:18, 21, 132-133), and the typed MintingScript is Constr 0 [B cs]. P21 (spending) and P7 (redeemer I 0) reject. Matches.

Policy flatten. seedelf.ak:28-30 and 51-53, `expect [(pid, tkn, amt)] = assets.flatten(mint)` (assets.ak:800-814, dict.foldr dict.ak:1125-1142): a right fold, policy-major, in map order, needing exactly one line across all policies. It matches flatLine, flatPairs and lineOf (definitions.lean:51-54, 106-113). Compiled flatten (seedelf.r.uplc:22-62): eager over the whole map, unBData on each policy, unMapData on each name map, each line List [B pid, name, amount]. Then exactly one line (:72-75/89, :94-97/129), and unBData on the name and unIData on the amount (:78-79, :100-101). Value is the raw List (Data × Data) encoded as Data.Map (V1/Value.lean:106-124). P6, P19 and P25 reject. P22, an empty name map under another policy that the ledger never makes, accepts on both sides. Matches.

Policy xor and strictness. logic.ak:8-22 matches (burn ∨ mint) ∧ ¬(burn ∧ mint) (definitions.lean:66). Builtin semantics matter for the policy. Under the pre-V3 variants A and B, consByteString wraps mod 256, and both P14 (a burn whose first input has index 256) and P16 (a mint whose name uses index 0 while the first input's index is 256) accept. seedelfName's `none` above 255 is right only under V3 semantics, which is what this V3 script runs under on chain. So policy_accepts_iff also depends on the Lean CEK using the V3 variant for consByteString. That is on the theorem's side, and I didn't check it.

The theorems count CEK steps (∃ n), not ledger ex-units. Measured on the deployed bytes: a Schnorr spend (W1) costs 336.8M CPU and 72.1K memory, about 3.4% and 0.5% of mainnet's per-transaction limits. A mint (P1) costs 21.4M and 72.8K. The budget can't flip a verdict for a transaction that declares enough ex-units, so I filed no finding.

Typed contexts are wider than the ledger's. Value is any List (Data × Data), ByteString is any String (chars can exceed 255), constructor tags and output indices are any Integer. On those values the definitions follow the compiled code: a name that isn't B rejects, and an empty name map (P22) accepts. The Aiken source gives them no meaning, because it trusts the ledger's types. No real transaction reaches them, so there is no source-versus-definition mismatch there.

Worth carrying into any claim, and already in policyAccepts: a burn also fails when the transaction's first input (inputs are sorted) has an output index of 256 or more, or when there are no inputs. That happens because xor evaluates the mint arm, whose consByteString aborts. A claim like 'any holder can burn' needs that condition; a user meets it by choosing inputs.

Two wallet behaviours that hold in both the source and walletAccepts: z_b with leading zero bytes is accepted, so the redeemer is malleable; and a UTxO whose datum isn't exactly Constr 0 [B, B] is spendable by anyone who sends a well-formed Proof and no signer.
A wording point, not filed: seedelfName's docstring says `none` comes from 'an index past 255', but negative indices also give none. No real transaction has a negative output index.

Not checked: whether every real ledger context lies in the image of IsData.toData (TxCert, governance and TxOut encodings, among others). The definitions read only the purpose, redeemer, datum, signatories, the first input's out ref and the mint, and I did check those encodings.

To find the deployed hex files I read the header of seedelf-verification/extract.sh and the module comment in Seedelf/Scripts.lean. extract.sh mentions a `git show` of 5b82530, but I ran no git command. I opened no proof, README, CLAIMS.md, docs or plans.
